A local Qwen dev (via dispatch.py) had rewritten the whole self-contained asset assets/backtotop.js to add the reading-progress ring but that run ended before committing, leaving it uncommitted in the working tree (HEAD still carried the original ring-less back-to-top; docs/ carried the old copy). PM adversarially VERIFIED the deliverable before adopting it: node --check passes; it references the required behaviors (scrollHeight/innerHeight, conic-gradient progress ring, requestAnimationFrame throttle, matchMedia prefers-reduced-motion, passive scroll/resize listeners) and pulls in ZERO external refs (no import/require/http/fetch/cdn); traced the rAF throttle (ticking flag set true after the guarded schedule) and confirmed it is correct (redundant re-set when already pending is harmless). What it does: the fixed bottom-right control now wraps the circular button in a thin masked conic-gradient ring whose fill is driven by a --p custom property recomputed as scrollY/(scrollHeight-innerHeight)*100 INSIDE the same single rAF-throttled update() (so it stays CWV-cheap and can't thrash layout), clamped 0-100 with a divide-by-zero guard for short pages; the control still only reveals (class is-visible) once scrollY > innerHeight, still restores keyboard focus toward the top on click, and — being injected entirely by JS — stays fully absent with no JS. PM wiring: none needed (the {scripts} slot already ships backtotop.js sitewide; the asset copytree carries the updated file into docs/). Validated end-to-end: build GREEN (11 guide pages + 3 posts = 17 HTML pages, BUILD_EXIT=0); all six build-time gates (internal-link, canonical, metadata, JSON-LD, sitemap, robots) still OK; full SEO gate GREEN on docs/index.html (exactly one <title>, one meta description, one rel=canonical, JSON-LD Article, exactly one <h1>) with sitemap.xml present; the rebuilt docs/assets/backtotop.js now carries the conic-gradient ring and byte-matches source; backtotop.js referenced on 17/17 pages.

done.changed: Local Qwen dev (via dispatch.py) authored improve/robotscheck.py — a pure, stdlib-only audit_robots(out_dir, base_url) that parses docs/robots.txt line-by-line (ignoring comments/blank/malformed lines), tracks User-agent grouping, and returns a list of {kind,loc,detail,severity} problems: errors for a missing file, no Sitemap: directive, a relative Sitemap URL, a Sitemap URL != BASE_URL/sitemap.xml, or a blanket 'Disallow: /' under 'User-agent: *' (which would deindex the whole site); a report-only warn when no Allow/Disallow rule is present at all. PM adversarially verified the logic against 8 objective fixtures (healthy pass; missing/relative/mismatched sitemap; blanket disallow under *; disallow-/ under a NON-* group correctly NOT flagged; missing file; no-rules warn — ALL_PASS), then wired the single audit_robots() call into build.py's main() right after the sitemap gate (the import was already present but the gate was never invoked — a dead check left by a prior run). Build stays green; docs/robots.txt passes; index.html retains its title/description/canonical/Article-JSON-LD/single-h1 invariants.

done.title: DEPTH: build-time sitemap integrity gate (improve/sitemapcheck.py) — parse docs/sitemap.xml, assert every <loc> is absolute + resolves to a real file, no duplicates, 404 never listed; report-only orphan-from-sitemap warnings.
done.changed: Local Qwen dev (via dispatch.py) authored improve/sitemapcheck.py — a pure, stdlib-only audit_sitemap(out_dir, base_url) that parses docs/sitemap.xml with xml.etree.ElementTree (returning a lone malformed_xml error if the file is missing or not well-formed, without raising), collects every namespaced <loc> by local tag name, and per loc runs ERROR checks: nonabsolute_loc (loc not under BASE_URL), listed_404 (loc resolving to 404.html), dangling_loc (absolute loc whose resolved on-disk file is missing) using the trailing-slash->index.html resolution rule, plus duplicate_loc (one per distinct repeated value). It also emits report-only orphan_from_sitemap WARNINGS: it walks docs/ for every *.html (skipping 404.html), maps each to its canonical URL exactly like canonicalcheck.compute_expected_url, and warns when an indexable page is absent from the sitemap. PM wired exactly two things into build.py (mirroring the linkcheck/canonical/metadata/jsonld gates): load sitemapcheck.py by path, and after the JSON-LD gate run audit_sitemap(OUT, BASE_URL), printing non-blocking orphan warnings and raising SystemExit(1) on any error. PM VERIFIED end-to-end: an OBJECTIVE fixture verify passed on attempt 2/3 (real docs/ sitemap -> 0 problems [no false positives]; a clean synthetic sitemap -> 0; a broken one flags exactly duplicate_loc/dangling_loc/nonabsolute_loc/listed_404 as errors + orphan_from_sitemap as a warn; a malformed sitemap -> malformed_xml error). Build GREEN (11 guide pages + 3 posts): the gate prints 'Sitemap audit: OK — every <loc> is absolute, resolves to a real file, unique, and 404-free (0 orphan warning(s)).' Full SEO gate GREEN on docs/index.html (exactly one <title>, one meta description, one rel=canonical, one <h1>, a JSON-LD Article node that parses, sitemap.xml present). LIVE negative test proved the gate bites: on the real docs/ audit_sitemap returns []; on a copy whose sitemap gained a dangling loc, a /404.html loc, and a duplicate loc it returns exactly ['dangling_loc','duplicate_loc','listed_404']. Sitemap correctness — a currently high-impact but previously unguarded crawl/index surface — can now never silently regress: a build can no longer ship a sitemap that is malformed, lists a dangling or root-relative URL, duplicates a loc, or exposes the 404 page to crawlers.

done.title: DEPTH: build-time structured-data integrity gate — a stdlib-only improve/jsonldcheck.py that, for every rendered page, parses each application/ld+json block (must parse), asserts the @graph contains an Organization, WebSite and Person node with the SAME stable @id used sitewide, and that every node's @id/url is absolute (starts with BASE_URL, never root-relative), so the entity graph can never silently fragment or drift to bad URLs.
done.changed: Local Qwen dev (via dispatch.py) authored improve/jsonldcheck.py — a pure, stdlib-only audit_jsonld(out_dir, base_url) that walks docs/**/*.html, extracts every <script type=application/ld+json> block and json.loads it (flagging kind='invalid_json' severity=error on any parse failure), flattens @graph / bare-object / list payloads into a node list, and for each page that carries JSON-LD asserts: (a) every top-level node whose @id or url is present is ABSOLUTE (startswith BASE_URL) else nonabsolute_id / nonabsolute_url (error) — the regression guard against root-relative entity URLs on the /seo-guide/ subpath deploy; (b) the graph contains at least one Organization, one WebSite and one Person node else missing_organization / missing_website / missing_person (error); and (c) sitewide consistency — it records each page's Organization/WebSite/Person @id, takes the most-common value as the canonical, and flags inconsistent_<type>_id (error) on any page whose core-entity @id drifts from it, so the connected entity graph can never silently fragment across pages.
